findings.title: The automated seed models language routes as separate pages
findings.impact: English and Norwegian counterparts are double-counted and would create an inflated, unstable translation scope.
findings.decision: Do not install the original seed. German Launch Baseline v1 uses 45 unique page concepts: 20 P0 and 25 P1.

findings.title: Redirect and counterpart routes were misclassified

routes.finding: redirect-only route incorrectly proposed as P0
actual Norwegian counterpart to /how-it-works incorrectly proposed as P2

findings.impact: The launch set would translate infrastructure while omitting a core commercial counterpart.
findings.decision: Exclude /no/product; map /no/slik-fungerer-det to the de-how-it-works P0 concept.

findings.title: The generated translation hashes are too broad and cross-locale

examples: /product includes English and Norwegian product content
slug collisions attach unrelated knowledge and research files
shared visual components are included in translation hashes

findings.impact: Unrelated design or Norwegian content changes can incorrectly mark German translations stale, while source ownership remains ambiguous.
findings.decision: Baseline v1 stores curated copy digests separately from implementation digests. DE Wave 5 must implement locale- and entry-aware stale detection.

findings.title: The source snapshot is not complete
findings.impact: The immutable commit is verified, but the packaged source snapshot omits a file central to locale routing.
findings.decision: No rerun is required for Wave 0 because the commit and manifest are immutable and verified. Add src/i18n/ and src/hooks/ to the next audit script snapshot allowlist.

findings.title: The current runtime architecture is binary English/Norwegian

examples: src/proxy.ts maps only /no to no and every other path to en
header/footer dictionaries are typed for current en/no locales
GlossaryLocale is defined as en | no

findings.impact: Creating /de pages without a shared locale registry would produce English locale state, scattered special cases, and fragile future expansion.
findings.decision: DE Wave 1 must introduce a generic locale/market registry before substantive German page production.

findings.title: Canonical and hreflang conventions are inconsistent

examples: Core pages mix no-NO and nb-NO
the Norwegian legal metadata helper does not emit a complete reciprocal set

findings.impact: Adding de-DE on top of inconsistent local metadata would multiply errors and make reciprocity audits unreliable.
findings.decision: Centralize metadata and standardize active language tags to en-US, nb-NO, de-DE and x-default in DE Wave 1.

findings.title: Two launch-adjacent English pages lack page-level metadata
findings.impact: The German implementation could inherit incomplete SEO foundations.
findings.decision: Keep /how-to-use in P0 and repair metadata. Hold /get-started outside the German launch set until the account/app journey is localized or the page is redefined.

findings.title: About and support may be overridden by production CMS content not captured in Git
findings.impact: The verified Git commit may not equal the text a production user sees.
findings.decision: Export and freeze the effective production CMS rows before translation; then make locale ownership explicit.

findings.title: Current legal copy is not ready for German publication

examples: English privacy and terms pages contain Effective Date: [Insert date]
Norwegian legal content labels itself launch copy and lists unresolved shipping, returns, withdrawal, complaints, processors and app-data details
The baseline Norwegian CE wording reflects an in-progress state and must be reconciled with the now-completed CE documentation

findings.impact: Literal translation would carry placeholders, stale status statements and incomplete market terms into Germany.
findings.decision: Treat German legal pages as market adaptation or German-native authoring, with separate legal and regulatory approval.

findings.title: US-specific FDA pages should not enter the German launch set
findings.impact: They add irrelevant launch work and confuse an EU/CE-focused German legal journey.
findings.decision: Keep FDA content available on existing languages but exclude it from German Wave 0/P0.

findings.title: Get started currently enters an English-only private account journey
findings.impact: A translated public page would hand German customers into an untranslated account flow.
findings.decision: Hold /get-started outside the initial German launch scope. Reintroduce it when the private account/app boundary is deliberately localized.

findings.title: Dynamic route patterns are templates, not translation concepts
findings.impact: Registering templates alongside generated routes creates duplicates and misleading coverage counts.
findings.decision: Track templates as implementation infrastructure; register exact published content entries as concepts.

findings.title: The shop page contains comparatively strong benefit claims
findings.impact: Direct translation may conflict with the intended-use and claims framework chosen for Germany.
findings.decision: P0 claims review is mandatory before German copy is drafted.
